verdicts.factCheck: Fetched this session. mega-evm main crates/mega-evm/src/block/limit.rs (1,080 lines, sha256 900012bc...) is byte identical to the cycle 21 copy in cycles/021/high-throughput.work/dl/mega/main-crates_mega-evm_src_block_limit.rs. pre_execution_check begins at line 765, and lines 881-889 return MegaBlockLimitExceededError::StateGrowthLimit whenever block_state_growth_used >= block_state_growth_limit, before execution and whatever the candidate would do. post_execution_update_raw (lines 942-943) adds the executed transaction's state growth with no check, so the transaction that reaches the limit is kept. Lines 33-38 state that a block-level violation means the transaction is skipped and the next one tried. constants.rs on main lines 206 and 211 set TX_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT and BLOCK_STATE_GROWTH_LIMIT to 1000. The resource limit specification at docs.megaeth.com says the first transaction that meets or exceeds a block-level runtime limit must be included, later candidates must be skipped before execution, a skipped transaction gets no receipt and may be reconsidered in a later block, and the gas limit must fit a sequencer-configured per-transaction gas cap. The page gives no order for reconsideration. On-chain: mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc answered mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42, block 32,885,578 has baseFeePerGas 1,000,000 wei and gasLimit 10,000,000,000, and blocks 32,885,500 and 32,885,510 are 10 seconds apart, so one block per second. At 22,559,525 gas per filler (the cycle 19 estimate, not re-run) one filler per block costs about 1.95 ETH per day, as stated.
verdicts.codeCheck: The PoolManager has no path that avoids the block limiter and no state that depends on block time or number. A grep of src/ for block.timestamp and block.number finds only src/test/NoDelegateCallTest.sol:8 and :12. A delayed transaction meets the same unlock gate and delta count check (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114), the same onlyWhenUnlocked modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:96-99), and the same modifyLiquidity, take and burn bodies (src/PoolManager.sol:145-184, 291-297, 332-336). Slippage limits belong to the caller's router, so a later price is bounded by the caller. No line of src/ moves value because of the skip.
verdicts.corrections: The skip is at limit.rs lines 881-889 inside pre_execution_check, which starts at line 765; the skip rule in the module comment is at lines 33-38. Delay of more than one block per filler for a chosen exit depends on the unpublished sequencer queue rule (operator), as the finding says. The 22,559,525 gas cost was not re-measured in this cycle.
